title: Rework benchmarking harness: consolidate load tests and perf-regression pipelines
creator: Priya Raman
body:
Background:
We have three overlapping benchmarking systems for inference: a legacy k6-based load suite used by the Serving team, a JMH-style micro-benchmark harness for hotpath kernels, and a Python-based perf-regression pipeline (evals runner) that measures quality vs throughput. These diverged over 2025–2026 with duplicated workloads, inconsistent configuration, and brittle CI hooks. The result is flaky alerts, opaque regressions, and high engineering overhead when updating models or runtime kernels.

Goal:
- Consolidate load and perf-regression tooling into a single maintainable harness with clear separation between production-like load tests and deterministic microbenchmarks.
- Reduce CI flakiness by adding stable baselines, deterministic seed control, and better resource isolation.
- Make it straightforward for infra/serving engineers to add new scenarios and for SRE/PM to understand perf regressions via standardized dashboards.

Scope of work (high level):
1) Extract the common runner layer (scenario definitions, sample workload generators, result schema) into a single repository `infra/bench-runner`.
2) Replace custom shell glue with a Python CLI that can target backends: k6 for high-concurrency load, the existing micro-benchmark harness for kernel-level tests, and a new headless executor for the evals pipeline.
3) Standardize metrics emitted (tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, memory RSS, GPU util, kernel-time) and wire to Prometheus + Grafana templated dashboards.
4) Add deterministic traffic replay mode (recorded traces + KV cache priming) to remove noise from perf-regression CI.
5) Migrate critical CI jobs: perf-regression (nightly), release-smoke-load (pre-release), and canary burn-in.
6) Provide migration docs and a small compatibility shim so existing scenarios continue to work during rollout.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Use Python for the orchestration layer to leverage existing evals code and ease onboarding; keep k6 for high-concurrency where JS-based checks are mature. This increases language mix but minimizes rewrite risk.
- Deterministic replay will require capturing representative traces; we will curate a small set of 10 golden traces per model family (LLM, reranker, embedder) — initial cost to capture, long-term stability benefit.
- We will not merge microbenchmarks into k6 because kernel-level timing needs tight host controls; instead the bench-runner will dispatch microbench jobs to the existing kernel harness.

Acceptance criteria:
- All existing high-importance scenarios (list attached) run end-to-end from the new bench-runner and produce the standardized JSON result schema.
- Nightly perf-regression CI job green for 7 consecutive runs (with established baselines) before we mark the old pipeline deprecated.
- Dashboards display historical baselines and alert thresholds; first set of alerts tuned with SRE.
- Migration doc + compatibility shim published in `docs/bench-runner-migration.md`.

Repos / artifacts to be modified:
- infra/bench-runner (new)
- infra/perf-ci (CI jobs)
- serving/benchmarks (scenario definitions migrated)
- evals/pipeline (executor integration)

Metrics baseline (example):
- Model: redwood/llm-prod-v2, seq_len 1024, batch=1
- Baseline p95 latency: 82 ms
- Baseline tokens/sec: 2400
- Acceptable regression threshold: +10% tokens/sec drop or +15% p95 latency increase

Migration plan / rollout:
Phase 1 (2 weeks): scaffold bench-runner repo, CLI prototype, and a POC replay mode using one golden trace.
Phase 2 (3 weeks): integrate k6 and microbench backends, create result schema, and emit to Prometheus. Migrate 3 critical load scenarios.
Phase 3 (2 weeks): migrate perf-regression CI, tune alerts, and run parallel comparison for 2 weeks.
Phase 4 (1 week): flip over, deprecate old pipelines, postmortem and follow-ups.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Resource contention during concurrent runs causing noisy metrics. Mitigation: CI will pin ephemeral nodes and use cgroups; initial runs use isolated runners.
- Risk: k6 behavior differs from previous JS harness. Mitigation: side-by-side validation with captured traces and runbook to debug mismatches.
- Risk: Too many metrics leading to alert fatigue. Mitigation: start with a minimal alerting set and iterate with SRE and PM.

Next steps (this ticket):
- Spike: bench-runner CLI and standardized JSON schema (Ethan) — PR opened.
- Capture golden traces for redwood/llm-prod-v2 and redwood/embedder-v1 (Marta) — task created.
- Update nightly perf-regression job to consume the new schema (Carlos) — blocked on infra/runner image.

Links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Bench+Runner+Proposal (internal)
- PR (prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/642 (WIP)
acceptance_criteria: New bench-runner runs existing high-priority scenarios and emits standardized JSON results
Nightly perf-regression CI stable for 7 consecutive runs after migration
Dashboards show historical baselines and alert thresholds for the migrated scenarios
Migration documentation and compatibility shim published
comments: 2026-02-25 Priya Raman: Created ticket after on-call flagged noisy perf alerts during the runtime-1.20 rollout. Initial triage shows three divergent harnesses.

2026-02-28 Ethan Cole: Spike complete — prototype CLI at infra/bench-runner; basic k6 glue works. Opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/642. Need to decide on result schema before wider migration.

2026-03-02 Marta López: Captured two golden traces for llm-prod-v2 and embedder-v1; uploaded to GCS bucket gs://redwood-bench/goldens/ (link in design doc). Found variance in tokenization boundary handling between current eval runner and serving runtime — added task ENG-4834.
2026-03-05 Carlos Mendes: Trying to update perf CI to consume new runner, blocked by missing runner image in infra registry. Filing dep ENG-4760 to build image and publish artifacts.

2026-03-09 Ethan Cole: Ran side-by-side comparison for 3 scenarios. microbench times aligned within 3% but load tests diverged due to connection pooling; adding connection priming step to bench-runner. Marked: In Progress.
2026-03-12 Priya Raman: Sync with SRE — agreed on minimal alert set for first migration (p95 latency and error rate). SRE to tune Prometheus rules next sprint.
